chapters.summary: This section emphasizes why graphs are useful: they display data visually, making interpretation and comparison easier. Three major graphical methods are introduced: (1) Bar Graphs – rectangular bars of equal width representing discrete categories; (2) Histograms – bars representing continuous class intervals without gaps; (3) Frequency Polygons – line graphs connecting class midpoints. Students learn how to choose scales, how to draw axes, how to represent frequencies, and how to interpret patterns from visuals. Real-life applications include analyzing surveys, representing school data, and visualizing statistical trends.

chapters.summary: Bar graphs are used for discrete data, histograms for continuous data, and frequency polygons for visualizing trends. Students learn to interpret heights, shapes, and clusters to understand real-world information.
